WHAT IS TRUTH TABLE?
A truth table is a table used in logic to show the truth values of logical expressions. It lists all possible combinations of truth values for the variables in the expression and the resulting truth value of the expression itself.

Negation
It reverses the truth value of a proposition.
Examples:
p: “It is raining.”
~p: “It is not raining.”
p: “I will not study.”
~p: “I will study.”
p | ~p
T | F
F | T

Conjunction (AND)
p | q | p ^ q
T | T | T
T | F | F
F | T | F
F | F | F
It is TRUE only when BOTH statements are true.
p: I will have salad for lunch.
q: I will have rice for dinner.
Therefore:
p ∧ q = I will have salad for lunch and rice for dinner.

Disjunction/ Inclusive OR
It is FALSE only when BOTH statements are false
p | q | p ∨ q
True | True | TRUE
True | False | TRUE
False | True | TRUE
False | False | FALSE
p: I will go to school.
q: I will stay home.
Therefore:  p v q = I will go to school or I will stay at home.
Note: This operation is also called inclusive or, because it includes the possibility that both p and q are true.

Exclusive OR
It is True if exactly one is true.
p | q | p ⊕ q
True | True | FALSE
True | False | TRUE
False | True | TRUE
False | False | FALSE
p: Switch A is ON.
q: Switch B is OFF.
This means: The alarm will not sound if:
Both Switch A and Switch B is ON.
  OR
Both Switch A and Switch B is OFF.

Conditional (Implication)
It is FALSE only when p is TRUE and q is FALSE
p: The car is Rolls-Royce.
q: Sarah will buy it.
Therefore:
p ⇒ q = If the car is Rolls-Royce, then Sarah will buy it. 🡺 TRUE
p ⇒ ~ q = If the car is Rolls-Royce, then Sarah will NOT buy it. 🡺 FALSE
p | q | p ⇒ q
True | True | TRUE
True | False | FALSE
False | True | TRUE
False | False | TRUE

Biconditional (If and only if)
It is TRUE when both values  are the same.
p: Today is Monday.
q: Tomorrow is Tuesday.
p | q | p ↔ q
True | True | TRUE
True | False | FALSE
False | True | FASLE
False | False | TRUE
p ↔ q = Today is Monday if and
only if tomorrow is Tuesday. 🡺TRUE
~ p ↔ ~ q = Today is not Monday,
so tomorrow is not Tuesday. 🡺 TRUE

Example:
p: The restaurant is open.
q: I have a reservation.
~p v q:
The restaurant is not open OR I have a reservation.

Truth table:
~p v q
p | q | ~p
True | True | False
True | False | False
False | True | True
False | False | True
~p | q | ~p v q
False | True | True
False | False | False
True | True | True
True | False | True

Example: Truth table:
(p ⇒ q) ⇒ (~q)
p | q | ~q | p => q | (p ⇒ q) ⇒ (~q)
T | T | F | T | F
T | F | T | F | T
F | T | F | T | F
F | F | T | T | T
